correctness.rationale: Every point of Hom(K_m,K_n) is uniquely an m-by-n stochastic row array with disjoint positive column supports. Sorting each row preserves all support cardinalities and is continuous. Equality of separately sorted row multisets allows the rowwise column bijections to assemble into a single target permutation, exactly classifying orbits. The sorted length-k row simplex has barycentric coordinates lambda_j=j(a_j-a_{j+1})>=0 summing to 1, with vertices v_j=(1/j,...,1/j,0,..). Positive support total <=n gives exactly the stated chamber union; the compact Hausdorff quotient therefore is homeomorphic. The nested simplices D_k intersect in common faces; positive compositions of n into m parts index maximal chambers of dimension n-m. Straight-line interpolation of each row toward v_1 stays in its original D_k and fixes the common vertex, proving strong contractibility for all integers in range. Independent m=3,n=5 check found 10 vertices and 6 maximal chambers.
residual_risks: This is an ordinary target-color orbit quotient, not Borel quotient or source-position symmetry.
